Treat the two conjuncts independently, using the defining property of Dirac probability measures.

For continuity, unfold `diracProbaEquiv`: its forward map is
\[
x \mapsto \langle \delta_x,\ \delta_x\in\operatorname{range}(\mathrm{diracProba})\rangle.
\]
Continuity into the range subtype reduces to continuity of \(x\mapsto\delta_x\) in the ambient weak topology on probability measures. Establish this through the topology’s test functions: for every bounded continuous \(f\),
\[
\int f\,d\delta_x=f(x),
\]
which is continuous in \(x\). The `OpensMeasurableSpace` assumption makes these test functions measurable; `T0Space` supplies the point-separation needed for the Dirac map to define the stated equivalence with its range.

For injectivity, suppose \(\delta_x=\delta_y\). If \(x\ne y\), `MeasurableSpace.SeparatesPoints` gives a measurable set containing exactly one of \(x,y\). Evaluating both measures on this set gives respectively \(1\) and \(0\), contradicting their equality. Thus \(x=y\).
